A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PANTHER study, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. Appendices A–D are retained unchanged; v2 inserts a NeurIPS checklist before them.

before.justification: v1 reports original WeChat Pay deployment experiments and public-benchmark results, plus efficiency, transferability and ablation experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original prediction, fraud-detection and recommendation results, including the online A/B test and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Structured tokenization, SPRM, user-profile contrastive learning, cached hybrid inference and merchant-risk scoring are unchanged. No algorithm, objective or model component is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use WeChat Pay, CCT, MBD-mini, MovieLens-1M and Yelp with the same prediction, fraud detection, merchant assessment, recommendation and transfer scenarios.

E2.justification: Transformer, SASRec, HSTU, DeepFM, DCN and TabBERT comparisons remain in their corresponding experiments. Appendix efficiency and transfer comparators are also unchanged; bibliography revisions do not change evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Chronological splits, full-ranking evaluation, metrics, the 10-day online A/B test and Appendix B training configurations are unchanged. The checklist refers to existing settings without revising the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Component ablations in Table 1 and Figure 4, prototype visualization in Figure 3, efficiency and transfer analyses in Tables 6–8, and loss-weight sensitivity in Table 9 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 already reports ± values in Tables 1–2 without defining them. v2 checklist item 7 identifies the reported uncertainty as standard errors from repeated experiments. This clarifies reporting but supplies no run counts or seeds and does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, WeChat Pay HR@1 remains 0.2452 ± 0.0005, and Figure 4 retains the 38.6% fraud-recall improvement at the top-0.1% threshold.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), SPRM complexity reasoning, merchant-risk definitions and Appendix A notation are unchanged. The checklist's statement that the paper has no theoretical results introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning behavioral pretraining, personalization, transfer and efficient deployment, including the same headline performance claims.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, interpretations of transfer and fraud-detection results, and the conclusion's interpretability limitation are unchanged. The checklist adds generic assurances and references existing discussions without developing new substantive limitations.

D1.justification: Section 4.1.1 changes the code location from yzhangjy/PANTHER to WeChatPay-Pretraining/PANTHER. The checklist also states that public-benchmark code was submitted and documented. Appendix B implementation, tokenization and compute details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Some cited sources change: the heterogeneous-GNN citation switches from Wang et al. (2019) on user-behavior prediction to Liu et al. (2018) on malicious-account detection. The related-work argument remains unchanged; HSTU deduplication and publication-metadata updates alone are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 adds a standalone NeurIPS checklist, cleans up references and makes small copyedits, including shortening a repeated SPRM expansion and removing a stray character. The scientific narrative and existing section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The checklist introduces question-and-answer pages between the references and appendices, while expanded bibliography entries cause local reflow. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–9 retain their designs, captions and organization; appendix pages are visually identical apart from page numbers.

improvement.justification: Defining the existing uncertainty estimates as standard errors and consolidating the duplicated HSTU reference modestly improve reporting and traceability. Scientific evidence remains unchanged. The gains are limited by unspecified run counts and the checklist's unsupported assertion that licenses are included in the otherwise unchanged appendices.
